_comment: Carry destination for issue #1398 (R6-D8-01, the no-hot-water dead-entities
finding). The fix made the hot-water family's registry default dynamic --
entity_registry_enabled_default is now a property conditional on dhw_enabled --
instead of a static _attr_entity_registry_enabled_default = False. The round-6
D8 finder's matrix harness still counts the static attribute, so its
no_dhw_gate_counts counter must be re-anchored when #1398 is re-verified.
Shape and required fields: .claude/rules/finding-propagation.md. Linted by
stage: the seat that re-verifies finding #1398 (a round-6 D8 verifier or judge, or the seat that commits the round-6 D8 matrix harness to the tree)

carries.from: the round-6 D8 fix for #1398, which replaced the static default-off with a dynamic entity_registry_enabled_default property on _DHWEntityMixin in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/sensor.py
carries.control: The finder's counter no_dhw_gate_counts counts _DHWEntityMixin entities where getattr(type(e), '_attr_entity_registry_enabled_default', True) is not False and not e.available. The fix no longer sets that static attribute on the five non-temperature hot-water entities, so the counter reads them as enabled-by-default and reports 5 for a no-hot-water install even though the dynamic default is off. The null control is the hot-water variant: with dhw_enabled True the counter reads 0 at both ends, which separates the dynamic fix from a blanket off.
carries.remeasure: Re-anchor no_dhw_gate_counts to read e.entity_registry_enabled_default (the dynamic property) instead of the static _attr_entity_registry_enabled_default, and re-run PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round6/D8/matrix.py at the head. d8_no_dhw_enabled_unavailable must move from 5 to 0 for a no-hot-water install, and stay 0 for a hot-water install.
carries.brief: The #1398 fix is dynamic, not static. The hot-water family's registry default is now the entity_registry_enabled_default property on _DHWEntityMixin, off only where dhw_enabled is False (no hot water) and on where hot water is configured, so a no-hot-water install ships no dead enabled entities while a hot-water install keeps the card plan and the Energy-dashboard DHW meters on. Do not read the static _attr_entity_registry_enabled_default: it is deliberately left unset on the five non-temperature entities, and the probe-gated DHWTemperatureSensor keeps its own static default-off, which is evidence about the probe, not about the rest of the family.
